Forwarding Aurora's markups. Key asks: additional insured naming, COI delivery timing (10 business days post-signature), and cyber $5M. Procurement wants a quick yes/no and any escalation path.

- We typically can provide additional insured for GL and Auto; endorsements on Tech E&O are more nuanced.
- COI delivery timing is usually 5–7 business days from our broker once order form is countersigned, but we have exceptions in a few enterprise deals.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood MSA — insurance section and COI

David / Aditya —

I reviewed Aurora's markups and drafted a short response. Main recommendations below (I also attached a tracked-changes PDF with our suggested wording).

1) Additional insured:
- We can commit to naming Aurora Systems as Additional Insured on Commercial General Liability and Automobile Liability via standard ISO endorsement CG 20 10/11 (or equivalent).
- For Technology E&O (Professional Liability), we cannot grant Additional Insured status because that endorsement is typically limited to vicarious liability scenarios and carriers push back. Instead propose: "Redwood will extend defense and indemnity obligations for claims arising out of Redwood's acts or omissions in connection with the Services."

2) COI timing:
- Standard internal practice: COI issuance within 7 business days post-execution. We can offer 10 business days only if Aurora accepts delivery via email to procurement@redwoodinference.com and acknowledges that delays from their broker may extend timelines.
- Proposed language: "Certificates of insurance shall be provided within 7 business days following execution of the Order Form; where a customer requires 10 business days, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to comply. Failure to deliver within the period shall not delay Order Form effectiveness but parties will remediate per the insurance cure process."

3) Cyber limits:
- Our baseline (hosted) cyber/tech E&O limit is $3M. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can consider $5M with an additional premium and review of scope.
- Proposed path: if Aurora requires $5M, Redwood proposes a SOW addendum specifying dedicated/private deployment or a shared-cost excess policy. We can include an SLA/financial assurance fallback.

4) Quick operational asks:
- Need Aurora's broker contact (name/email) so our broker can begin endorsement coordination.
- Please confirm whether Aurora wants carrier-to-carrier confirmation or if a COI + endorsement is sufficient.

I can push a short reply to Maya with this framing if you sign off.

Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_ins_comments_v1.pdf, COI-template.pdf

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — insurance section and COI

Maya —

Thanks for the markups. Quick summary of Redwood's position and next steps below (Kimberly copied for legal language):

- Additional Insured: We can add Aurora as Additional Insured on GL and Auto with the standard endorsement. We cannot provide Additional Insured on Technology E&O; instead propose the defense/indemnity language Kimberly suggested.
- COI timing: Our normal delivery is 7 business days; we can accommodate 10 business days if Aurora accepts emailed delivery and acknowledges broker timing risk.
- Cyber limits: Standard is $3M. If Aurora requires $5M, we can do that for Dedicated/Private deployments or via an excess policy at cost-share.

Operational asks: please confirm Aurora's broker contact and whether carrier-to-carrier confirmation is required. For transparency, attaching our COI template (COI-template.pdf) and a clean version of our proposed language. If we get broker contact today, we'll engage our broker and aim to produce endorsements/COI within 5–7 business days of countersignature.

Proposed next step: Maya signs off on acceptance of the E&O fallback language and confirms broker name/address; Procurement can then finalize the Order Form schedule for signatures.

If that works I can have our legal team issue the redline response by EOD.

Best,
David
